items.text: The artist is relieved and fixes the obvious mistakes.
The artist is offended, then admits that the hat really was a bit much.
The revised portrait looks even less like the Chief. Everyone agrees to stop while they are ahead.
The children love the portrait. The Chief slowly grows fond of it.
The Chief accepts the joke with dignity, but requests a less prominent location.
The portrait becomes a famous village curiosity.
The artist explains a thoughtful symbolic choice that the audience had misunderstood.
The artist says, "The enormous nose represents wisdom." The Chief replies, "Does it."
The artist admits (artist.he/she) simply cannot draw noses.
The portrait hangs in a quiet corner, where visitors occasionally stop to admire - or question - it.
The artist and Chief share a laugh after the crowd leaves.
A child produces a much better drawing in five minutes. The artist asks for lessons.
The Chief privately admits that the portrait captures something true, even if the nose is unforgivable.
The portrait is put away carefully, not destroyed. Someday it may be a cherished reminder of this moment.
a nose of astonishing proportions
a magnificent mane of hair that the Chief does not possess
an expression of profound constipation
six fingers on one hand
an enormous ceremonial hat that nobody has ever seen
a tiny body and an inexplicably enormous head
a suspicious resemblance to the artist's pet lizard
a heroic pose that makes the Chief look ready to attack the sun

intro_a1.name: The commission
intro_a1.text:
The villagers have decided to commission a portrait of their Chief to commemorate an important achievement.
The Chief {politely objects|pretends not to care|is secretly thrilled|worries the whole thing is unnecessary}.
The artist, (Artist), is {a talented but impatient adult|a shy apprentice|an elder with a very distinctive style|a Master Builder who has never painted anything in (artist.his/her) life}.
When the portrait is unveiled, it depicts the Chief with {PROBLEM1}.

dec1.text: The Chief thanks the artist and asks for a small revision.

dec2.text: The Chief displays the portrait proudly, flaws and all.

dec3.text: The Chief declines to display it publicly but keeps it as a gift, explaining the choice kindly.

dec4.text: The Chief declares that the village needs fewer portraits and more benches. The artist offers to paint a bench.
